decisions.why: FR-003 both halves. The wording now says what the previous review asked: the inlined script gains an indexing branch that is inert where no group carries data-in, so a hamlet page draws, counts and behaves as before (FR-008). Confirmed in the plan text and in page.js (the branch reads data-in only when present).

decisions.why: FR-002 with FR-006 and the spec's Decisions Recorded row for rooms.

decisions.why: Ruled LEGITIMATE last round on the measured audit (identical output on all six sheets; the fold only removes artifacts of the room rects FR-002 forces; no finding hidden). The plan's figure is now Ubame +1/-1, matching that run.

Hand-run browser probe over the five pages written into research.md; unit tests for reader, page and registry, including a standing test over sheet.pieces() of the three hand sheets holding each part's kind and parent; no browser test.
decisions.why: SC-001/SC-002 name a probe; the standing test (test_every_part_is_its_own_kind_and_lights_with_its_parent, tests/interactive/test_compound_kinds.py) enforces FR-001, FR-003 and FR-009 and is enforcement of the request, not unrequested scope. Confirmed present.

decisions.summary: The id map palette gains a green channel past 63 kinds (first 63 keep their red-only colors and keys); page.js reads both channels; data-in is written after data-k so raster._GROUP still finds a part's group.
decisions.why: Both halves are required for FR-001/SC-001 in raster mode: with data-in before data-k every part fell out of the id map and named its parent (R4), and Ubame's 69 kinds exceed the 63-entry palette so its page could not be written at all. Read in raster.py: classes 1-63 keep color #RR0000 and key str(red), so a hamlet id map (under 63 classes, green always 0) and its palette are unchanged, and page.js returns the same key for a green-0 pixel. FR-008 holds.

decisions.summary: The id map renders text unblended (--text-rendering optimizeSpeed) on the magistracy pages.
decisions.why: FR-001/SC-001: with blended glyph edges Ubame's fox-relics label answered as the shrine altar (19 vs 688 pixels, R4), i.e. a part named another kind. The picture a reader sees is not the id map, so FR-006 is untouched.

decisions.summary: The same flag applied unconditionally, so every hamlet page's embedded id map and its raster-mode label hit-testing change ('Every label on every page now answers on its whole glyphs', hamlets included).
decisions.why: The accepted spec says FR-008 'The hamlet pages MUST be unchanged'; the plan and R4 say outright that hamlet pages change (page.py embeds raster.id_map output in every page, and the flag in raster.id_map is unconditional). That makes FR-008 'unchanged, except the id map's text', a carve-out the spec does not carry and the GM's request does not reach: the request is about magistracy parts and never mentions hamlets. None of the tests passes. It is not impossible to keep hamlets unchanged: the flag can be applied only where the defect bites (for example only when render_page is given within=, or only on compound pages). The GM's words do not imply it. Keeping hamlets unchanged does not defeat the request, which D11a already serves. Constitution XIV (fix a defect where you find it) does not rescue it as a plan decision. The hamlet defect is ASSERTED, not measured: R4 measures only Ochiba and Ubame, both magistracies. And a fix that breaks an accepted MUST goes through a spec amendment reviewed against the request, not a plan line. Remedy, either one: (1) scope the flag so no hamlet page's id map changes, and correct the plan's D11 sentence and R4's 'hamlets included'; or (2) measure the defect on a hamlet page, amend FR-008 and SC-005 to admit the id-map text fix as a XIV defect fix, have the amendment reviewed, then re-run this plan review.
